words.definition: A body of water partly enclosed by land, smaller than a gulf.
A large body of salt water, smaller than an ocean.
A raised piece of land, smaller than a mountain.
A large body of water surrounded by land.
A hill of sand formed by the wind, often found in deserts.
A ridge of rock, sand, or coral near the surface of the sea.
A large natural hole in the side of a hill or under the ground.
A steep, high rock face, often found along a coast.
A small, narrow stream.
A large area of sea partly surrounded by land, bigger than a bay.
A low, wet area of land, often covered with grass.
An open area of land, often used for farming.
A place where people live, smaller than a city.
A path built for vehicles to travel between places.
An open area of land used for recreation.
The land along the edge of an ocean, sea, or lake.
The direction toward the top of a map, opposite of south.
The direction toward the bottom of a map, opposite of north.
A long, narrow raised strip of land or mountains.
A small open area within a forest.
Another word for a small island.
A steep, rugged rock or cliff.
A large, open area of rough grassland, often wet, common in cool climates.
A poetic word for a valley.
One of the seven huge landmasses on Earth, such as Africa or Asia.
One of the five huge bodies of salt water that cover most of Earth.
A very high area of land with steep sides, higher than a hill.
A large natural stream of water flowing toward a sea, lake, or another river.
The low area of land between hills or mountains, often with a river running through it.
A mountain with an opening that can erupt hot lava, ash, and gas.
A huge, slow-moving mass of ice found in cold mountain or polar regions.
A piece of land almost surrounded by water but connected to a larger landmass.
The imaginary line around the middle of the Earth, halfway between the North and South Poles.
The city where a country's government is based.
The line that separates one country or region from another.
One half of the Earth, such as the Northern or Southern half.
A large area of flat land with few trees.
A large area of flat, high land.
A group or chain of many islands.
A shallow area of water separated from the sea by a sandbar or reef.
A cold, treeless region near the Arctic where the ground stays frozen.
A flat grassland found in warm regions, especially Africa.
A dense forest that gets very heavy rainfall all year.
The outline of land where it meets the sea.
An area of land controlled by a particular country or ruler.
The distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees.
The distance of a place east or west of a fixed starting line, measured in degrees.
A book of maps.
A narrow strip of land connecting two larger areas of land.
The flat, triangular land formed where a river splits into smaller streams before reaching the sea.
A long, narrow inlet of the sea between steep cliffs, formed by glaciers.
A narrow channel of water connecting two larger bodies of water.
One of two lines of latitude marking the edges of the warm equatorial zone.
A low area of land where water collects, often drained by a river system.
An isolated hill or mountain with a flat top and steep sides.
A vast, dry, grassy plain found in Europe and Asia.
A fertile, green spot in a desert where water is found.
A ring-shaped coral reef or island surrounding a lagoon.
The wide part of a river where it meets the sea and fresh water mixes with salt water.
A large area of flat or rolling grassland, especially in North America.
The physical features of an area of land.
A long chain of mountain ranges.
A smaller river or stream that flows into a larger one.
An area of land where all the water drains into the same river or lake.
A layer of soil that stays frozen all year in very cold regions.
A strong seasonal wind that brings heavy rain to parts of Asia.
The shape and features of the land's surface in a particular area.
A region of the world that follows a single standard time.
A very large and busy city.
The remote areas of a country, away from the coast or major cities.
A large landmass that is part of a continent but distinct from it, like India.
A steep slope or cliff that separates two flatter areas of land at different heights.
Places on opposite sides of the Earth from each other.
A gentle, sloping region of land found at the base of a mountain range.
A landscape formed by the dissolving of soft rock like limestone, often full of caves.
A large, compact group of mountains forming a single geological unit.
A fine, wind-blown soil that forms fertile plains.
Fine soil and sediment left behind by flowing water, often forming fertile land.
The process where one tectonic plate is forced underneath another.
The gradual wearing away of land by wind, water, or ice.
The process by which material carried by wind or water is laid down on land.
The scientific study of water movement and distribution on Earth.
The science and practice of drawing maps.
The process by which fertile land turns into desert, often due to drought or poor farming.
The process by which more people come to live in cities rather than rural areas.
One of two days a year when day and night are of equal length everywhere on Earth.
One of two days a year with the longest or shortest period of daylight.
To sail or travel all the way around something, especially the Earth.
The single supercontinent scientists believe existed before today's continents drifted apart.
words.riddle: Long ago, all the continents were joined as one giant landmass. What was I called?

words.definition: An ancient southern supercontinent that eventually broke apart into Africa, South America, and other landmasses.
An ancient northern supercontinent that later split into North America, Europe, and Asia.
Crossing or extending across an entire continent.
The marking of the boundary or limits of an area.
The act of a country adding new territory to itself, often by force.
The act of settling among and establishing control over people in another area.
Originating naturally in a particular place; native.
